market_holds: Spot $4.78 at the 18:10 UTC seal ($4.87 on the 16:00 bar): -8.1% over 5 days, -12.8% over 20 days, -53% over 60 days, 1% above the 52-week low and 67% below the high. Front-week options price a 14.1% event move net of ordinary volatility (16.2% straddle, ATM IV 165%, 22% spread). The last 8 reactions had a median of 4.1% and a max of 8.8%, and 3 of 8 were up. Most of the 60-day fall is the sector tape: APLD -46%, CRWV -43% and IREN -61% over 60 days on Yahoo bars, and DUOT has tracked them day by day. The company-specific part is about Oct 7-14, after the Oct 5 sale of the GPU cluster SPV: DUOT -39% against APLD -20% and IREN -26%. Consensus (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-10) is Q3 revenue about $12.8M and EPS about -$0.01, FY26 revenue $55.5M. The company guide is FY26 revenue above $50M and positive adjusted EBITDA, last reaffirmed 2026-10-05. Targets from the Q2 call (2026-08-17): Q4 recurring infrastructure revenue $17-18M, an exit run-rate above $70M at margins above 70%, Q4 adjusted EBITDA $8-10M, and a 2027 framework of at least $160M. Short interest was 6.1M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (about 19% of the 31.5M shares outstanding on the Q2 10-Q cover), 11.5 days to cover. Put/call open-interest ratio 0.83. The stock trades on whether the AI-colocation pivot produces revenue and margin, i.e. the Q4/FY guide, EBITDA and financing, more than on the Q3 headline.
view: Q3 is the first quarter that has to show the pivot, and three things since the last call make the print harder to read and probably weaker than the August framework. (1) Revenue mix. About $2.9M a quarter of related-party services revenue (the New APR asset-management agreement) was explicitly residual in Q1-Q2, with accelerated deferred-revenue recognition, and the agreement is winding down after New APR's assets were sold on 2026-05-26 (Q2 10-Q). So Q3 has to reach the $12.8M consensus from technology-solutions deliveries and Columbus hosting/GPUaaS alone, up from $3.3M of non-services revenue in Q2. That is possible: the Columbus site was expected to bill from August and 7 MW was installed by Oct 20. But this company has slipped against its own marks before: FY25 came in at $27.0M after a $28M pre-announcement, the guide went from $50-55M to 'above $50M', and Q1-26 and Q4-25 missed. (2) Economics. On Sep 30 Duos sold the GPU SPV (288 B300 servers) to Axe Compute for assumption of $87.8M of debt plus a $42.9M deferred price. It had $68.8M of equipment deposits on its June balance sheet, so a GAAP loss on the sale is plausible (my estimate, not disclosed). It now leases the GPU capacity back from Axe and still covers colocation and energy. That turns GPU depreciation, which adjusted EBITDA excludes, into a lease cost it includes, so the August Q4 targets ($8-10M adjusted EBITDA, more than 70% margins) look hard to keep as stated, though gross revenue can survive. (3) Capital. Contracts for 55 MW (Axe) and 20 MW (a cloud provider, Q2 2027) plus about 100 MW of land need far more capital than the June $112M cash minus Q3 build-out. The 'GPU senior debt' is moot after the sale, the Axe JV equity ($140M) is subject to financing, and this stock has fallen on financing news before. Against all this: the stock sits at a 52-week low with a market cap of about $150-155M, near cash plus the Axe receivable. Short interest is about 19% of shares. The sector is already washed out. Management is promotional and has paired prints with contract headlines (Q2 +12.8% on the 55 MW Axe deal). A reaffirmed FY guide plus any financing or site news could squeeze it. Net, I lean modestly down, with a large two-sided move, but I cannot see the line itself (Q4 guide, EBITDA reset, financing) and the downside is partly in a price that already fell 39% on the SPV sale.
unpriced: Possibly a stale Q3 revenue consensus (probably set before the SPV sale and the end of the New APR services stream; I could not date the revision) and stale Q4 EBITDA targets that rest on owning the GPUs. I cannot show that the price does not already hold this: the 39% fall after the Oct 5 sale, against about 20-26% for peers, may be exactly this re-rating.

recommendation.reason: The evidence points modestly down: the services revenue is gone, GPU economics changed under the lease-back, a likely loss on the SPV sale, a history of revenue slippage, and capital needs. But the price already fell much faster than peers after the SPV sale, short interest is about 19%, and the stock trades near cash plus the Axe receivable. The deciding lines (Q4/FY guide, EBITDA reset, financing) are not visible before the release, so I am well short of 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reaffirmed FY revenue guide above $50M with Q4 adjusted EBITDA targets kept despite the lease-back, plus funded build-out (Axe JV equity or non-dilutive debt) announced with the print: that against a 19% short interest would send it up hard.

self_critique: The bearish inputs (services gone, lease-back margins, financing need) are public, and the stock fell 39% in a week after the SPV sale while peers fell 20-26%, which is a plausible pricing of exactly these. The stock is near cash plus receivables, short interest is about 19%, and management reliably pairs prints with contract headlines, so any reaffirmation or financing win could squeeze it 15-25%. Overnight AI-infra sentiment may also swamp the release. My lean is thin, so no recommendation.
